examples.description: Move the next draft to 1 Aug 2026 (12:00 UTC of that date)
End the template after its invoice dated 31 Aug 2027 (12:00 UTC of that date)

preconditions: next_due is epoch millis: the daily run at 16:30 UTC (00:30 in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur) makes the draft invoice on the calendar day next_due falls on in the business time zone (sales_settings.timezone, unset = Asia/Singapore), dated that day; a day the run missed is made at the next run, still dated that day. For a date, send 12:00 UTC of that date (30 Sep 2026 = 1790769600000): it falls on that date in every listed zone, while 00:00 UTC falls on the day before west of UTC.

tax_scheme sg_gst or my_sst makes each invoice under that scheme at the rate in force on its issue day, each line taxed by its items_json tax_code (sg_gst default standard; every my_sst line needs one); "none" prices by tax_rate_bps; unset takes your sales settings' tax_scheme on each run. ends_on (epoch millis, the last day an invoice may be dated) and max_invoices (invoices in all) end the template: after its last invoice the run makes no more. A run that cannot make the invoice makes nothing, keeps the template due and says why in invoice_reminders_due (recurring_held). Nothing is ever sent: each invoice is a draft listed there under issues.

A null leaves a field as it is, so an end, once set, is moved rather than removed: send a later ends_on or a larger max_invoices (up to 1000). To skip one invoice without editing the template, call invoice_recurring_skip.

description: Update a invoice_recurring you own (optionally compare-and-set via expected_updated_at).

expected_updated_at.description: Optional compare-and-set guard: the updated_at you last read. Mismatch returns CONFLICT with the current value.

name: invoice_recurring_update
